status: draft-v4 (internal assistive; a human reviewer is the final authority)

defaults.perspective_preference: Mutual reciprocal (mNDA): both Parties are Disclosing and Receiving; positions are symmetrical. Amperesand drafts on its Singapore mNDA paper, with each protection running to whichever Party is the Disclosing Party in a given disclosure.
defaults.forum: SIAC arbitration under prevailing SIAC Rules, seat Singapore, single arbitrator, English; court carve-out for injunctive/equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction
defaults.term_standard: Agreement term 1 year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice (template Clause 8).
defaults.survival_standard: Confidentiality obligations survive for 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets remain protected for as long as they constitute trade secrets (template Clause 8). The trade-secret tail is template-standard; an executed deal that drops it (e.g., a counterparty form omitting the trade-secret sentence) is a deviation, not the standard.
required_carveouts: prior_possession (already in the Receiving Party's or its Representatives' possession/known before disclosure)
public_domain (is or comes into the public domain through no fault or breach by the Receiving Party or its Representatives)
third_party (received from a third party not known to be under any confidentiality obligation)
independent_development (independently developed, on its own or jointly, without regard or reference to the Confidential Information)
written_authorization (approved for release or use by written authorization of the Disclosing Party)
counsel_must_confirm: Confidentiality-survival standard = 2 years from the Effective Date + perpetual trade-secret tail (template Clause 8). Executed forms with 3-year flat survival and no trade-secret tail or with the trade-secret sentence dropped are deviations recorded as fallbacks.

Survival runs from the Effective Date on the template; a 2-year survival on a 1-year term yields an effective ~1-year post-expiry tail. Optional forward-looking improvement: re-anchor survival to termination/expiry or per-disclosure (an executed deal re-anchored to 'termination of discussions' which is more protective for Amperesand as discloser).

Singapore-law mNDA uses SIAC arbitration seated in Singapore with an injunctive-relief court carve-out (template Clause 16). Counterparty SG paper sometimes substitutes exclusive Singapore-court litigation (no arbitration) - acceptable fallback on Singapore paper; foreign-law/foreign-seat substitutions are not.

PDPA (Personal Data Protection Act 2012) governs any shared personal data swept into Confidential Information under limb (c) of the definition; confirm PDPA handling/transfer-limitation where personal data is exchanged.
Electronic Transactions Act 2010 (Singapore) is the e-signature statutory basis on SG paper; ensure no ESIGN/UETA (US) or jury-trial-waiver boilerplate bleeds in from counterparty US forms.
ADOPTED (pending counsel): perpetual/uncapped trade-secret carve-out is the standard default; confirm approved language and that it is not silently dropped in negotiation.

positions.title: Definition of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information means any and all information relating to the Purpose disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party that is marked or communicated as confidential, including (a) business/affairs/customers/suppliers/plans/market-opportunity information and IP/operations/processes/product/know-how/technical/designs/trade-secrets/software of the Disclosing Party and its subsidiaries, (b) information/findings/data/analysis derived from the Confidential Information, (c) any shared personal data, and (d) other information identified as confidential at disclosure, including third-party confidential information held by the Disclosing Party; PLUS a reasonable-person catch-all sweeping in unmarked information apparent to someone familiar with the subject area as the type typically treated as confidential, or that the Receiving Party has reason to believe may be confidential, with NO marking requirement and NO oral-to-writing confirmation deadline (template Clause 1).
walk_away_triggers: Definition hard-scoped to a single technology, sample, or category so that Amperesand's broader shared information (financials, strategy, personnel, customers, OPS/power-electronics designs) falls outside protection where Amperesand is the primary discloser of IP.

Asymmetric, counterparty-only expansions of CI scope not mirrored for Amperesand (e.g., a fund's investment strategies/portfolio deemed confidential; a strategic OEM's prototypes/samples auto-deemed that party's CI regardless of marking) - resist unless reciprocal.

Runaway scope beyond the Purpose or beyond formal disclosure: 'whether or not related to the project' / 'in the ordinary course of business' / constructive or inferred-knowledge catch-alls (observation/overhearing) that create inadvertent-breach exposure for Amperesand as Receiving Party.

Retroactive capture of pre-agreement disclosures with no time limit combined with broad catch-alls ('whether furnished on, before or after the Effective Date' - observed on some executed paper) - cabin to disclosures made for the Purpose.

Subjective 'by its nature' or 'would significantly harm the legitimate business interests' catch-all with no marking safe harbor and the burden on the Receiving Party to prove non-confidentiality (observed on an executed counterparty form) - scrutinize when Amperesand may be recipient.

MNPI / securities-trading acknowledgment folded into the definition that imposes affirmative internal-compliance and personnel-advisory duties on Amperesand (observed on investor paper re: parent-company securities) - push out of scope or cabin.
acceptable_fallbacks: A marking/'reasonably should know' construct (counterparty paper) where unmarked information still qualifies if the recipient knew or reasonably should have known it was confidential - acceptable provided no fixed oral-to-writing memorialization deadline is imposed on Amperesand's oral disclosures.
A broad 'Authorised Representatives' chain (shareholders, affiliates, related companies, advisers) on counterparty SG paper, provided the Receiving Party remains fully liable for all of them.
Express inclusion of the existence/terms of the Agreement and the fact of negotiations as Confidential Information (more protective; acceptable and consistent with template intent).

positions.title: Permitted Purpose
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information may be used and disclosed solely for a single, narrowly defined 'Purpose' stated in the recitals - exploring a potential business relationship between the Parties (or a potential investment into Amperesand) - and for no other purpose (template recitals + Clause 4 use limitation).
walk_away_triggers: Investor/fund 'investment management' or portfolio carve-out expanding permitted use to evaluating other investments (including Amperesand competitors) using Amperesand's CI - strike or ring-fence.

Purpose extending beyond evaluation to ongoing 'business activities arising from the relationship,' permitting open-ended operational use of CI without a separate definitive agreement - limit to evaluation only.
Disclosing-party-controlled open-ended catch-all ('and other purposes as allowed by the disclosing party') giving the counterparty unilateral expansion of permitted use - strike.

Anti-reverse-engineering / design-around prohibition embedded in the use/purpose clause broad enough to constrain Amperesand's own legitimate independent engineering on overlapping subject matter (observed as a reverse-engineer/derivative-works ban on investor paper) - narrow to misappropriation of disclosed CI only.
Unfilled bracketed/placeholder Purpose language left in an executed agreement creating scope ambiguity - do not sign until the Purpose is finalized to one complete definition.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 'potential investment / strategic corporate transaction' framing for investor counterparties (observed on investor paper) so long as use is confined to evaluating that transaction.
A sector-specific Purpose recital (e.g., 'Onshore Power Supply (OPS) solutioning' on a strategic-OEM counterparty's paper) - acceptable and in fact narrows scope favorably.

positions.title: Exclusions from Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: Five exclusions: prior possession; public domain (no fault/breach); third-party receipt (no known confidentiality duty); independent development (without regard or reference to the CI); approved-for-release by written authorization. Compelled disclosure is handled separately as Required Disclosure (Clause 3), not as a sixth exclusion (template Clause 2).
walk_away_triggers: Independent-development carve-out entirely absent - exposes Amperesand to confidentiality/IP entanglement on its own R&D that overlaps a counterparty's CI.
Prior-possession / prior-knowledge carve-out entirely absent - Amperesand could be bound on information it already held before disclosure.
Severely truncated carve-out set (only two or three) where prior possession AND independent development are both missing.

Subjective or distorted carve-out tests that defeat legitimate exclusions - e.g., third-party receipt conditioned on the recipient's knowledge of the transferor's 'improper action,' or a public-domain test drafted as 'through Receiving Party breach only' that fails to cover information already public at disclosure.
No compelled-disclosure mechanism (information neither carved out nor covered by a Required Disclosure clause), leaving Amperesand unable to comply with a court/regulatory order without breaching.
acceptable_fallbacks: An independent-development carve-out limited to development 'by Covered Persons / Representatives' without use of or reference to the CI (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.

Folding compelled/legally-required disclosure into the exclusions list as a carve-out (observed on a counterparty's executed paper) PROVIDED it still requires reasonable prior notice and compliance with protective orders - acceptable as a structural variant.
A 'reasonably demonstrable' prior-possession standard placing a light evidentiary burden on the recipient (observed on investor paper) - acceptable if not extended to all carve-outs.

positions.title: Confidentiality Obligations
positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party holds all Confidential Information in strict confidence, does not disclose it to any third party without the Disclosing Party's prior written approval, uses it solely for the Purpose, applies at least the same degree of care as for its own confidential information of like importance (but never less than reasonable care), limits access to Representatives (directors, officers, employees, advisers) strictly on a need-to-know basis, remains fully responsible for its Representatives' breaches and takes reasonable measures to restrain them, and promptly notifies the Disclosing Party of any loss or unauthorized disclosure - on a mutual/reciprocal basis (template Clause 4).
walk_away_triggers: Prior written consent of the Disclosing Party required before the Receiving Party may make ANY copies of Confidential Information (impedes ordinary review/use) - resist (observed on a counterparty CNDA limiting copies to those 'necessary' for permitted disclosures).
Oral/visual disclosures protected only if reduced to writing and marked within a fixed deadline, risking loss of protection for Amperesand's own oral disclosures - refuse.
Broad commercial-use or 'no use/exploitation for any commercial purpose without written approval' restriction exceeding the Purpose limitation - refuse.

Reverse-engineering / design-around / derivative-works use-restriction broad enough to bind Amperesand's INDEPENDENT development, with no independent-development carve-in (observed on fund paper) - resist or carve out.

Expanded disclosee universe letting the counterparty share Amperesand's CI with its investors / portfolio companies / investment group without a direct confidentiality obligation (observed: an investor's affiliated investment-group disclosure right; fund 'portfolio companies' activities) - require consent and direct confidentiality flow-down.

Mandatory affirmative-enforcement obligation requiring the Receiving Party to take 'all steps the Disclosing Party may require' or use 'best endeavours' / 'all reasonable measures including court proceedings' against its own Representatives at its own cost (observed on an executed counterparty form) - push back.
Requirement that each Representative individually execute identical written undertakings before any access as a mandatory obligation on the Receiving Party (operationally unworkable) - refuse.
Securities-trading / MNPI affirmative-compliance obligation or AI-training prohibition bolted onto the confidentiality clause - refuse or scope-limit/reciprocate.
acceptable_fallbacks: 'Same degree of care... but no less than a reasonable degree of care under the circumstances' (counterparty wording) - equivalent to template and acceptable.
Representative undertakings satisfied by 'agreed in writing or otherwise have an obligation' to keep confidential (observed on investor paper) rather than fresh signatures - acceptable.

An option (not obligation) for the Disclosing Party to require Representatives to enter a confidentiality agreement in an acceptable form (observed on a strategic-OEM counterparty's paper) - acceptable as a Disclosing-Party right.
A controlled investment-group disclosure pathway gated on the disclosing party officer's written approval (observed on investor paper) - acceptable only with the consent gate intact.
An affirmative enforcement obligation against the Receiving Party's own Representatives is acceptable only as vicarious liability, not mandated litigation/best-endeavours.

positions.title: Permitted Disclosures (Representatives and Compelled)
positions.standard_position: The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information (a) to its Representatives on a need-to-know basis for the Purpose, remaining responsible for their compliance, and (b) where compelled by a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority with jurisdiction (and, on Singapore paper, a relevant exchange regulator), provided it (i) gives reasonable prior written notice to the extent not legally prohibited, (ii) discloses only the minimum legally required, and (iii) uses reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment, with prompt post-hoc notice if advance notice was impossible - all rights mutual/symmetrical (template Clauses 3 and 4).
walk_away_triggers: One-sided affiliate-, supplier-, or investor-network disclosure rights letting the counterparty push Amperesand CI to its affiliates/suppliers/investment group without Amperesand's consent and with no reciprocal right (observed: a unilateral affiliated-investment-group disclosure right).
Disclosure to open-ended classes such as 'prospective co-investors,' 'potential sources of financing,' or 'current and/or prospective investors' without consent.

Mandatory obligation to 'provide all assistance and take such steps as the Disclosing Party may reasonably require to prevent or minimise' a compelled disclosure, ceding control of Amperesand's response to legal process (observed on an executed counterparty form) - cabin to reasonable cooperation at the requesting party's cost.
Shifting the cost of resisting/limiting compelled disclosure onto Amperesand as Disclosing Party as a baseline term.
Requiring prior written notice to the counterparty before the Receiving Party may share with its OWN need-to-know Representatives - operationally unworkable.
Broad non-announcement/non-publicity clause barring even acknowledgment that discussions exist, where it could constrain Amperesand's legitimate investor or regulatory communications.
acceptable_fallbacks: A general-regulatory-request carve-out allowing the recipient to respond to routine regulator requests (e.g., MAS/FTC/DOJ/SEC) without notice, provided the request is not specifically focused on the Disclosing Party or the subject matter (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.
A securities-law/stock-exchange-regulation exception to the non-disclosure of the existence/terms of the Agreement (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.

'Reasonable notice before disclosure and compliance with any applicable protective order' (observed on investor paper) - acceptable; functionally the template's notify/minimize/seek-confidential-treatment set.

positions.title: Required Disclosure
positions.standard_position: Where the Receiving Party (or its Representative) is obligated or requested to disclose Confidential Information by a valid court order or governmental/regulatory authority, it must (i) to the extent not legally prohibited, give the Disclosing Party reasonable prior written notice, (ii) disclose only the Confidential Information required, and (iii) use reasonable efforts to ensure confidential treatment; if it cannot notify before disclosure, it must, to the extent permitted by law, inform the Disclosing Party of the full circumstances and information disclosed as soon as reasonably practicable (template Clause 3).
walk_away_triggers: No compelled-disclosure / Required-Disclosure mechanism at all, leaving Amperesand unable to comply with a court or regulatory order without breaching the NDA.

Obligation to 'provide all assistance and take such steps as the Disclosing Party may require' to prevent/minimise disclosure, effectively ceding control of Amperesand's response to legal process to the counterparty (observed on an executed counterparty form) - cabin to reasonable cooperation.
Fixed long advance-notice periods (e.g., 30 days) that cannot be met under urgent court/government orders.
A regulatory carve-out so narrow it omits subpoenas/court orders, or that strips the notice/minimization protections.
acceptable_fallbacks: Compelled disclosure structured as a carve-out within the exclusions list (observed on a counterparty's executed paper) rather than a standalone clause, PROVIDED the notice and protective-order obligations remain.

'Prompt notice of the existence, terms and circumstances' plus reasonable steps to minimise scope (counterparty SG wording) - acceptable once 'all assistance/all steps as required' is softened to reasonable cooperation.

positions.title: Term and Confidentiality Survival
positions.standard_position: The Agreement commences on the Effective Date and expires 1 year from the Effective Date, terminable earlier by either Party on written notice. Confidentiality obligations survive any termination/expiration for 2 years from the Effective Date; trade secrets remain protected for as long as they constitute trade secrets (template Clause 8).
walk_away_triggers: No post-termination survival at all, or confidentiality co-terminous with a (potentially very short) agreement term, leaving disclosed information unprotected once the term ends or definitive documents are signed.

Flat survival measured from the Effective Date that equals or is shorter than the agreement term, producing zero or near-zero post-expiry protection, with NO trade-secret carve-out (observed: 3-year flat survival, no trade-secret tail, on fund house paper).

Perpetual or indefinite survival imposed on Amperesand when Amperesand is the RECEIVING party - including open-ended 'as long as it qualifies as confidential under applicable law' tails and perpetual retained-copy/backup carve-outs.

Internally contradictory or ambiguous survival drafting (or a spelled-out number disagreeing with its parenthetical figure) that a court could read as either expiring with the agreement or as perpetual - fix to a clear finite period before signing.

Drop of the trade-secret tail in an Amperesand-paper deal where Amperesand is the primary discloser of technical IP (observed: an Amperesand SG form executed with the 2-year survival sentence but WITHOUT the trade-secret continuation) - reinstate the trade-secret tail.
acceptable_fallbacks: 5-year per-disclosure survival measured from receipt of each item (observed on a US investor CNDA) - acceptable and in some respects more protective than a 2-year flat tail.
3-year flat survival from the Effective Date (observed on fund house paper) - acceptable as a fallback only if paired with a trade-secret carve-out; resist the no-trade-secret version.

Survival re-anchored to 'termination of the Parties' discussions' rather than the Effective Date (observed on an executed counterparty form: 2 years from termination of discussions) - acceptable and more protective for Amperesand as discloser.

positions.title: Survival of Obligations
positions.standard_position: Each Party's rights and obligations regarding Confidential Information survive any termination or expiration of the Agreement for the confidentiality-survival period (2 years from the Effective Date), with the trade-secret tail surviving for as long as the information qualifies as a trade secret; surviving obligations are independent of the agreement term (template Clause 8).
walk_away_triggers: Survival provision that lets the obligations lapse entirely on termination of the agreement term, with no independent survival of confidentiality.

Survival keyed to retention period of backup/archived copies such that obligations effectively extend indefinitely for any retained data when Amperesand is the recipient (observed: 'such information retained... will continue to be subject to the terms... for such period that the Recipient retains such information' on an executed counterparty form).
Ambiguity over which clauses survive (a bare 'this section survives' list that omits the core confidentiality obligations).
acceptable_fallbacks: An explicit enumerated survival list of the confidentiality and miscellaneous clauses (observed on investor paper) - acceptable provided the core confidentiality and use-restriction clauses are included.

positions.title: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information
positions.standard_position: On the Disclosing Party's written request or upon expiration/termination, the Receiving Party must within 14 days return or destroy (at its election) all documents and tangible materials representing the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information and all copies, except it may retain one (1) archival copy (including automatic archiving/back-up records) solely to perform surviving obligations and as required by law, court, regulator, or internal audit/compliance procedures, with the Agreement continuing to apply to any retained copy (template Clause 7).
walk_away_triggers: Retention satisfied by reference to the Receiving Party's own record-retention schedule or internal document-retention policy, letting the counterparty keep Amperesand CI for as long as its policies permit (observed: 'in accordance with its policies and procedures' on one form; 'in accordance with the internal document retention policies of the Recipient' on another) - renders the destroy obligation illusory.

Broad carve-out permitting retention of derivative work product - notes, summaries, memoranda, board/approval papers, analyses - so that materials derived from Amperesand CI need not be returned or destroyed (observed: an executed counterparty form's carve-out for papers submitted to its board/executive committee).
Open-ended/indefinite retention of backup or archival copies with no sunset and a perpetual confidentiality tail, especially where it effectively negates destruction of all ESI.
Blanket right for a counterparty's professional advisers to retain copies per their own practice, untethered from a specific legal requirement.
Return-only obligation with no destruction option and no certification mechanism, forcing physical return of all ESI.

Loss of any trigger for return on demand - e.g., obligation arises only on a 'decision not to proceed' with no right for Amperesand to demand return at any time or on expiry (a template-Clause-7 protection is the on-demand AND on-expiry trigger).
acceptable_fallbacks: A single archival copy retained 'for use solely in the event of a dispute' and to establish legal/regulatory compliance, remaining subject to the confidentiality provisions (observed on investor paper) - acceptable, tighter than the template's law/audit retention.
A routine-IT-backup exception to the destroy obligation (observed on investor paper) - acceptable where the backups remain subject to confidentiality.
A certification-of-destruction requirement (observed on investor paper) - acceptable and in fact a stronger control than the template; adopt where offered.

positions.title: No Transfer of Rights, Title, or Interest
positions.standard_position: The Disclosing Party retains all right, title and interest in its Confidential Information (including copies and extracts) and grants no licenses or rights except as expressly set forth; nothing grants any license to, or waiver of, any patents, copyrights, trademarks, or mask works (template Clause 10).
walk_away_triggers: Any IP assignment, vesting, or work-for-hire obligation requiring Amperesand (as recipient) to assign IP, inventions, or 'derivatives of Confidential Information' it creates - strike or carve out Amperesand's pre-existing and independently developed IP.
A patent-filing prohibition barring Amperesand from filing applications relating to information it receives - resist or narrow.

'Derived directly or indirectly' or 'in the course of interaction' IP-capture language sweeping in Amperesand's own innovations that merely touch counterparty information - require a clear carve-out for pre-existing/independently developed/residual-knowledge IP.
Any provision deeming disclosure an implied license or waiver of patent/copyright/trademark/mask-work rights, or granting the recipient an affirmative license to the discloser's IP.
acceptable_fallbacks: A 'No License' clause requiring any license to be express and in a separate signed document (observed on investor paper) - acceptable and equivalent to template intent.
An express statement that Confidential Information 'remains the exclusive property of the Discloser' (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.

positions.title: No Warranty / No Other Obligations
positions.standard_position: Confidential Information is provided AS-IS with no representation or warranty (express or implied) as to accuracy, completeness, or fitness; the Disclosing Party is under no obligation to supply any particular Confidential Information; and neither Party is obligated to enter into any transaction, with no partnership/JV/agency created and each Party free to terminate discussions at any time (template Clauses 6 and, by negotiation practice, an AS-IS disclaimer; counterparty forms add an express warranty disclaimer).
walk_away_triggers: A consequential/indirect/special/punitive damages waiver or liability cap bundled into the no-warranty clause that would limit Amperesand's recovery (including lost profits and fees) when a counterparty misuses Amperesand's CI - if it must remain, carve out confidentiality breaches and IP misappropriation from the waiver (observed: a broad 'Damages' exclusion on US investor paper).
A one-directional damages exclusion or non-reliance limitation protecting only the counterparty as discloser while leaving Amperesand fully liable as discloser - require mutuality.
Any affirmative warranty by Amperesand beyond a narrow right-to-disclose (warranting accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, fitness, or performance of Amperesand's CI) - refuse.
A no-warranty clause coupled with an indemnity on Amperesand for the counterparty's use of or reliance on the disclosed information - refuse (indemnity in an NDA is dealbreaker-class).
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual express AS-IS warranty disclaimer (observed on investor paper and an executed counterparty form) - acceptable and improves on the template's implicit position.
A 'each Discloser warrants only that it has the right to disclose' representation (observed on investor paper) - acceptable as the sole permitted warranty.
A mutual no-reliance / no-obligation-to-transact provision (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.

positions.title: Remedies / Injunctive Relief
positions.standard_position: Each Party acknowledges monetary damages alone may be insufficient for a breach and agrees the Disclosing Party (in a mutual NDA, either Party as Disclosing Party) may seek specific performance or injunctive relief from any court in any jurisdiction, as a non-exclusive remedy in addition to all other remedies at law or equity, with no bond requirement and no cap on monetary damages (template Clause 12).
walk_away_triggers: Recipient must waive all rights to oppose injunctive/equitable relief sought by the Disclosing Party (blanket pre-emptive waiver of Amperesand's defense rights when Amperesand is the recipient) - refuse.
A low/fixed bond cap (e.g., a nominal dollar ceiling) that a court could read as limiting relief or security - refuse any numeric bond cap.
Broad mutual waiver of consequential/special/punitive/exemplary damages materially capping Amperesand's recovery for misuse of IP.
Injunctive relief narrowed to IP-rights infringement only, excluding ordinary confidentiality breaches.
Complete omission of any injunctive-relief/irreparable-harm clause, leaving Amperesand without an express equitable-remedy acknowledgment.
Injunctive/no-oppose right made one-sided in the counterparty's favour in a mutual NDA.
Indemnification or uncapped damages liability bundled into the remedies clause beyond standard NDA scope.
acceptable_fallbacks: Remedy framed as available to 'the injured Party' rather than only 'the Disclosing Party' (observed on investor paper) - acceptable and mutual.
Express statement that equitable relief is non-exclusive and in addition to all other remedies (observed on investor paper) - acceptable, matches template.

positions.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
positions.standard_position: Governed by the laws of Singapore. Disputes referred to arbitration administered by the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) under its prevailing rules, seat Singapore, single arbitrator, conducted in English, with a court carve-out limited to injunctive/equitable relief (template Clause 16 + Clause 12).
walk_away_triggers: No governing law and no dispute-resolution/forum clause at all, leaving applicable law and enforcement uncertain.
Governing law specified but NO forum or dispute mechanism - insist on a clear court or arbitration forum.

Wholly foreign, non-home legal regime with foreign-seat litigation/arbitration giving the counterparty home-court advantage (e.g., a foreign national law with a foreign arbitral seat or foreign-court forum) - refuse or escalate.

Counterparty home-forum lock with exclusive jurisdiction and consent to personal jurisdiction at the counterparty's domicile (observed: exclusive Delaware Chancery jurisdiction on US fund paper, with broad waiver of inconvenient-forum/venue objections) - refuse a one-sided home-forum lock when Amperesand has no nexus.

Mixed/inconsistent template: a foreign-law (e.g., Delaware) contract embedding operative Singapore statutory definitions (PDPA, Companies Act, Electronic Transactions Act) with no conflicts carve-out - fix before signing.
US-litigation boilerplate (jury-trial waiver, US-state exclusive courts) inserted into a Singapore-governed agreement, or vice versa - strike as inapplicable.
acceptable_fallbacks: Singapore law with exclusive jurisdiction of the Singapore courts (litigation, no SIAC arbitration) on counterparty Singapore paper (observed on an executed counterparty form) - acceptable on Singapore paper; the home law/forum is preserved.

On counterparty US investor paper, Delaware law with Delaware courts (non-exclusive jurisdiction, observed on investor paper) is a more acceptable fallback than exclusive Delaware Chancery jurisdiction (observed on other investor paper); resist the exclusive-Chancery lock.
SIAC seated in Singapore but administered under ICC rules, or a neutral third-country seat, for a sophisticated cross-border counterparty - acceptable per-deal.

positions.title: Assignment
positions.standard_position: Neither Party may assign rights or delegate obligations without the other Party's prior written consent, except that (i) the Disclosing Party may assign to an acquirer of substantially all of its assets by operation of law, and (ii) Amperesand (Party A) may assign to any Affiliate on prior written notice only (no consent required); any purported assignment in violation is null and void, and assignment does not relieve the assignor of its obligations. 'Affiliate' means an entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with a Party (template Clause 15).
walk_away_triggers: Agreement freely binding on 'successors and assigns' with no consent or notice requirement, allowing either party to assign automatically (e.g., on a counterparty's acquisition), transferring access to Amperesand's CI to an unknown third party.

Counterparty granted a unilateral right to assign to its affiliates/subsidiaries freely or in M&A without consent, while Amperesand needs the counterparty's consent - asymmetry running against Amperesand.
In a mutual NDA, the assignment restriction framed only against the 'Recipient,' leaving the Discloser (either party) free to assign without consent.
M&A/change-of-control carve-out with a one-sided non-competitor restriction applying only to Amperesand's acquirer.
No assignment clause at all, leaving assignment to permissive local-law defaults that could let the counterparty assign without Amperesand's consent.
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual right for EITHER party to assign to its wholly owned affiliates (observed on investor paper) - acceptable; symmetric and consistent with the template's Affiliate-assignment intent.

A flat 'no assignment without prior written consent of the other Party' with no carve-outs (observed on an executed counterparty form) - acceptable, though it removes Amperesand's notice-only Affiliate-assignment right; add the Affiliate carve-out if negotiable.
Disclosing Party's assignment to an acquirer of substantially all assets by operation of law (template) preserved on counterparty paper - acceptable.

positions.title: Residuals / Competitive-Use
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO residuals clause and NO competitive-use carve-out; the recipient must keep Confidential Information confidential and use it solely for the Purpose, with no right to use memory-retained 'residuals' or to apply Confidential Information to evaluate, develop, or invest in competing products or companies.
walk_away_triggers: Broad residuals clause permitting use of information retained in the unaided memory of representatives for any purpose / in the ordinary course of the counterparty's business.

Competitive-use or investment-management carve-out expressly permitting a counterparty (and its affiliates/portfolio companies) to use, fund, or invest in companies competitive with Amperesand (observed on investor paper: a fund 'portfolio companies... in competition with... the Company' non-restriction; an 'invest in multiple competitors with similar or identical strategies' acknowledgment).

Non-restriction / anti-exclusivity clause leaving a counterparty free to evaluate, acquire, or independently develop competing technologies or products (observed on investor paper: 'evaluating, acquiring from third parties, or independently developing... similar... technologies or products').
Any residuals or employee-reassignment clause lacking an express prohibition on direct use of Confidential Information.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrowly framed non-exclusivity / multiple-investments acknowledgment for an institutional investor counterparty ONLY where it is expressly conditioned on no Confidential Information being used or disclosed in those competing activities (observed on investor paper: 'provided that none of the Confidential Information is disclosed in connection therewith') - acceptable as a documented fallback on investor paper, NOT as Amperesand-standard language.
A residuals clause is otherwise unacceptable; the only fallback is the CI-ring-fenced non-exclusivity acknowledgment above.

positions.title: Non-Solicitation
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO standalone non-solicitation covenant. An NDA is a confidentiality instrument, not a trade-restraint vehicle. An inserted non-solicit is treated as a prohibited, high-severity, walk-away clause.
walk_away_triggers: Any standalone non-solicitation covenant untethered from use of Confidential Information.
Non-solicit period exceeding 12 months, or with no fixed term / perpetual restraint.
Unilateral / one-way non-solicit binding only Amperesand.
Non-solicit lacking a general-advertising and non-targeted-recruiting carve-out.
Customer/supplier non-solicit broad enough to restrain ordinary business (a de facto non-compete).
Liquidated-damages or indemnity tied to a non-solicit breach.
acceptable_fallbacks: A narrow, use-tethered, MUTUAL non-solicit (<=12 months, with a general-advertising carve-out) may be entertained only as a documented fallback on counterparty paper - not as Amperesand-standard language.

positions.title: Non-Competition
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's template contains NO non-competition clause; an NDA should remain a confidentiality instrument only. Preferred position: no non-compete, no non-compete-taint restriction, and no non-compete waiver in either direction.
walk_away_triggers: One-sided non-compete-taint / 'residual contamination' restriction imposed only on Amperesand that bars Amperesand personnel exposed to a counterparty's CI from working on competing technology - a de facto non-compete on Amperesand's engineering teams.
Broad definition of 'competes' tied to a personnel-segregation or taint obligation that can sterilize Amperesand's own R&D roadmap.

Non-compete waiver extracted from Amperesand requiring it to acknowledge a counterparty (e.g., a fund) may invest in, consult for, or service Amperesand competitors, with no reciprocal protection and no CI-use safeguards.
Any asymmetric non-compete obligation binding only Amperesand in a mutual NDA.
Any actual non-compete (restraint on Amperesand competing or soliciting) embedded in the NDA.
acceptable_fallbacks: A mutual non-exclusivity acknowledgment that does NOT restrain either party (the inverse of a non-compete) is acceptable only where CI use is ring-fenced; see the residuals position.

positions.title: Indemnification
positions.standard_position: Amperesand's standard NDA contains NO indemnification, hold-harmless, or fee-shifting provision; confidentiality breaches are remedied through general-law damages and equitable relief. Preferred position: strike any indemnity or attorneys'-fees clause entirely.
walk_away_triggers: Uncapped, one-way indemnity running only against the Recipient for any breach; if unavoidable, demand mutuality, a liability cap, and exclusion of indirect/consequential loss.
Legal/attorneys' costs recoverable on a solicitor-client / 'indemnity basis' rather than reasonable party-and-party costs.
Indemnity or liability extending to 'attempted or threatened' disclosure and to a broad list of affiliates, agents, advisers, shareholders, officers, and directors as indemnitees.
Uncapped explicit damages liability for unauthorized use/disclosure with no limitation of liability.
Any non-mutual fee-shifting or indemnity running only in the counterparty's favour.
Indemnity lacking carve-outs aligned to the confidentiality exclusions (compelled disclosure, independently developed information, publicly available information).
acceptable_fallbacks: Each party bears its own costs/expenses of discussions and negotiations (observed on investor paper) - acceptable; this is the opposite of fee-shifting and consistent with no-indemnity.

positions.title: Notices and Miscellaneous Boilerplate
positions.standard_position: Notices effective on delivery by hand, email, or certified/registered mail to specified addresses; clean boilerplate (no-publicity, no-waiver, severability, entire agreement/merger, written-signed amendments, counterparts, PDF/e-signature execution) with the e-signature statutory basis matched to governing law (Electronic Transactions Act 2010 on Singapore paper) and no extra regulatory obligations (template Clauses 5, 9, 11, 13, 14, 17).
walk_away_triggers: Incomplete or blank counterparty notice details (placeholder name/title/email) left in an executed agreement, undermining valid service of notices - never sign with placeholder notice fields.

Securities-trading / MNPI acknowledgment imposing affirmative internal-compliance and personnel-advisory obligations beyond an NDA's scope (observed on investor paper: a securities-law acknowledgment; a code-of-conduct provision) - push back as out-of-scope or accept only as a no-action awareness notice.
Attorneys'-fee / prevailing-party fee-shifting not in Amperesand's standard - resist or strike.
US-litigation boilerplate (jury-trial waiver) inserted into a Singapore-governed agreement where it is inapplicable and signals counterparty drafting control - strike as inapplicable.

A 'click-through supersession' / data-room provision that voids ab initio any other confidentiality agreement Amperesand's Representatives accept (observed on investor paper) - scrutinize; ensure it does not waive protections Amperesand relies on elsewhere.
Perpetual / unlimited-in-time survival of personal-data or other miscellaneous obligations - cap to a defined term.

A 'no modification or this Agreement is void' pre-signed lock (observed on a pre-signed counterparty CNDA: 'any modification will render this CNDA and the counterparty's signature null and void') that forecloses negotiation - accept only if the terms are otherwise acceptable as-is, never as a reason to sign deficient terms.
acceptable_fallbacks: Notice by personal delivery / courier / registered mail / electronic means with deemed-receipt timing (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.

Third-party-beneficiary exclusion ('made for the benefit of the parties... shall not benefit, or be enforceable, by anyone else,' observed on an executed counterparty form) - acceptable and consistent with the template's sole-benefit clause.
A no-publicity clause requiring Disclosing-Party written approval for any release/announcement (template Clause 5) - retain; it is an Amperesand-favorable protection.

positions.title: Entire Agreement and Amendments
positions.standard_position: The Agreement is the final, complete, and exclusive agreement on its subject matter, superseding and merging all prior discussions; no modification or amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties (template Clause 14).
walk_away_triggers: An entire-agreement clause that purports to supersede other signed agreements between the parties (e.g., a separate license or supply agreement) rather than only prior discussions on the same subject matter - cabin to the NDA's subject matter.
Amendment permitted by unilateral notice or by conduct rather than a writing signed by both parties.
A merger clause that disclaims reliance so broadly it could waive Amperesand's confidentiality protections established elsewhere.
acceptable_fallbacks: An entire-agreement clause that expressly preserves other signed NDAs/agreements as separate agreements (observed on investor paper) - acceptable.
A simple 'no addition/deletion/modification effective unless in writing and signed by the Parties' (observed on an executed counterparty form) - acceptable, equivalent to template.

positions.title: Personal Data / PDPA (Singapore)
positions.standard_position: Any shared personal data is swept into Confidential Information (template definition limb (c)) and handled under Singapore's Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA): collected/used/disclosed only for the Purpose, protected with reasonable security, not transferred outside Singapore except on PDPA-compliant terms, and returned/destroyed under the return-destruction clause. The SG mNDA does not contain a standalone DPA; personal data rides the confidentiality regime.
walk_away_triggers: A foreign privacy regime (e.g., US state privacy law) imposed as the governing personal-data standard on a Singapore-governed agreement, creating jurisdictional ambiguity over the applicable privacy regime - clean before signing.
Affirmative data-protection obligations (breach-notification timelines, audit/inspection rights, security-remediation at Amperesand's expense) bolted on one-sidedly - reciprocate or scope-limit.
Personal-data obligations with perpetual/unlimited survival - cap to a defined term.
Onward cross-border transfer of shared personal data without PDPA-compliant safeguards.
acceptable_fallbacks: A standalone, mutual data-processing addendum referencing the PDPA where significant personal data is exchanged - acceptable if reciprocal and term-limited.
Reliance on the template's confidentiality regime alone (limb (c)) where only incidental personal data is involved - acceptable.
